title: Author Guidelines
excerpt: Formatting, length, citation and anonymity requirements for every manuscript submitted to MOS Legis.
content:
Manuscript preparation

Manuscripts must be submitted in .doc or .docx format, in Times New Roman 12pt with 1.5 line spacing, and footnotes in Times New Roman 10pt with single spacing.

  • Research Articles: 5,000–12,000 words including footnotes
  • Short Articles and Essays: 2,500–5,000 words
  • Case Comments and Legislative Comments: 2,000–4,000 words
  • Book Reviews and Notes: 1,500–3,000 words
  • Book Chapters: as agreed with the Editorial Board

Abstract and keywords

Every submission carries an abstract of not more than 250 words and between four and six keywords. The abstract must state the question, the argument and the contribution, and must not be a summary of the literature.

Anonymity

The manuscript file must not carry the author's name, institution, acknowledgements or self-identifying citations. Author details are captured separately in the submission portal so that peer review remains double-blind.

Citation

Citations follow the MOS Legis citation format, with pin cites for every judicial authority. Parallel citations are given in the order set out in the style sheet and must be used consistently throughout.
seo_description: Formatting, length, citation and anonymity requirements.

title: Aim & Scope
excerpt: What MOS Legis publishes, the disciplines it covers and the standard against which submissions are judged.
content:
Aim

MOS Legis exists to publish rigorous, accessible legal scholarship that a court, legislature or practitioner could act on, without confining that scholarship to any one jurisdiction or school of thought.

Scope

The Review accepts work across the whole of legal study, including:

  • Constitutional and administrative law
  • Criminal law and procedure
  • Commercial, corporate and securities law
  • Dispute resolution and arbitration
  • Technology, data protection and privacy
  • Environmental and public policy law
  • Comparative, international and human rights law
  • Jurisprudence, legal history and legal writing

Standard

A manuscript is judged on originality, rigour, clarity and utility. Doctrinal, empirical, comparative and theoretical methods are all welcome provided the method is stated and followed.
seo_description: What MOS Legis publishes and the standard against which submissions are judged.

title: Peer Review Policy
excerpt: The double-blind review process, its stages and the timelines the Review commits to at each stage.
content:
Process

Every manuscript passes through pre-screening, plagiarism screening, editorial desk review and double-blind peer review by at least two reviewers with subject expertise.

Timelines

The Review commits to the following indicative timelines:

  • Acknowledgement of receipt: 2 working days
  • Pre-screening decision: 7 working days
  • Peer review outcome: 4 to 6 weeks (3 working days under Priority Review, where available)
  • Publication after acceptance and payment: 2 weeks

Decisions and reviewer notes

Decisions are accept, accept with minor revisions, revise and resubmit, or reject. Written reviewer notes accompany every decision, including rejections. Reviewer identities are never disclosed to authors.
seo_description: The double-blind review process, its stages and timelines.

title: Publication Ethics
excerpt: Authorship, conflict of interest, correction and retraction standards binding on authors, reviewers and editors.
content:
Authorship

Authorship is limited to those who made a substantial intellectual contribution. Ghost, gift and guest authorship are prohibited. All co-authors must be declared at submission; co-authors cannot be added after acceptance.

Conflicts of interest

Authors must disclose funding, employment, advisory roles and any involvement in litigation bearing on the subject of the manuscript. Editors and reviewers recuse themselves where a conflict exists.

Corrections and retractions

Errors that do not affect the argument are addressed by a published correction. Fabrication, falsification, undisclosed duplicate publication or established plagiarism results in retraction, with a retraction notice permanently attached to the record.

Simultaneous submission

Manuscripts under consideration elsewhere may not be submitted to the Review. Authors must withdraw formally before submitting a manuscript to another journal.
seo_description: Authorship, conflict of interest, correction and retraction standards.

title: Plagiarism Policy
excerpt: Similarity thresholds, the screening tool used and the consequences of an adverse plagiarism finding.
content:
Screening

Every manuscript is screened before peer review. The plagiarism screening fee is the only charge payable before an editorial decision; all other fees fall due only after acceptance.

Thresholds

Similarity is assessed excluding quoted matter, references and standard legal phrases.

  • Up to 10 per cent: proceeds to review
  • 10 to 20 per cent: returned to the author for revision before review
  • Above 20 per cent: rejected without review
  • Any verbatim uncited passage, irrespective of percentage: rejected

Consequences

A finding of plagiarism after publication results in retraction and notification of the author's institution. Screening fees are not refundable in any circumstance.
seo_description: Similarity thresholds and the consequences of an adverse finding.

title: Privacy Policy
excerpt: What personal data the platform collects, why it is collected, how long it is kept and the rights available to you.
content:
Data we collect

We collect only what the editorial process requires:

  • Account data: name, email address, mobile number, affiliation and author tier
  • Submission data: manuscript files, declarations, correspondence and review records
  • Payment data: transaction references only — card and bank details are held by the payment processor, never by the Review
  • Technical data: log and device information used to keep the platform secure

Use and disclosure

Personal data is used to operate peer review, publication, payment and notification. It is never sold. It is disclosed only to reviewers on a blinded basis, to service providers under contract, and where required by law.

Retention and your rights

Submission records are retained for seven years for editorial-integrity purposes; published records are permanent. You may request access, correction, deletion of non-published data, or withdrawal of consent by writing to the editorial desk.
seo_description: What personal data the platform collects and how long it is kept.

title: Terms & Conditions
excerpt: The terms governing use of the platform, submission of manuscripts, payment of charges and licensing of published work.
content:
Use of the platform

Accounts are personal and may not be shared. You are responsible for the accuracy of every declaration made in the submission portal and for all activity under your account.

Charges and refunds

Applicable charges are those published on the Fees & Pricing page on the date of submission. Plagiarism screening fees are payable upfront and are non-refundable. Publication charges fall due only after acceptance and are refundable only where the Review is unable to publish an accepted manuscript.

Licence

Authors retain copyright in their work and grant the Review a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to publish, archive, index and distribute it. Published articles are free to read.

Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of India and the courts at Mumbai have exclusive jurisdiction.

title: Disclaimer
excerpt: The Review publishes scholarship, not legal advice. This page sets out the limits of what publication implies.
content:
No legal advice

Nothing published by MOS Legis constitutes legal advice or creates an advocate-client relationship. Readers must take independent advice before acting on anything published here.

Views of authors

Views expressed in articles, blogs and comments are those of their authors alone. Publication does not indicate endorsement by the Review, its Editorial Board, its patrons or its partner institutions.

External links and listings

Job postings, career listings and external links are provided for information. The Review does not verify, endorse or accept responsibility for the content, accuracy or conduct of third parties.

title: Best Paper Winners
content:
How Winners Are Chosen

Each quarter, the editorial board selects one published manuscript as the Best Paper of the quarter, on the recommendation of the assigned reviewer and a final board vote.

The Prize

The winning author receives a certificate of recognition and a featured citation on the journal’s home page. A cash prize may also be awarded for the quarter.

Be Considered Next Quarter

Every manuscript accepted and published in a given quarter is automatically eligible. To be considered, simply submit your manuscript for publication.
